html:
The Totorames were an Indigenous people of the Pacific coast of northwestern Mexico, in what is now southern Sinaloa and northern Nayarit, around Chametla and the coastal lagoons. Little is known of them.

They farmed maize, fished in the rich lagoons and estuaries, and lived in sizeable towns. The conquistador Nuño de Guzmán marched through their land in 1530 and 1531. War, slaving and new diseases followed, and the Totorames disappeared as a people within a few generations, as the coast became part of New Spain. Their neighbours in the mountains inland were the Cora.
